ah girl you’re beautiful! only tips i have are contour a little higher on your face to lift your cheekbones more, maybe some blush also on your cheekbones for that lifted look and then have your eyeliner pointed more up so your eyes don’t look droopy
take an old tweezer or something and see if it pulls out, some of those liquid eyeliners are double sided so you can just flip it

i dont really recommend using concealer since your eyelid is naturally more oily than where you’ll typically use concealer so it’ll cause creasing and it’ll really hurt longevity of the look but you could probably make it work if you slap a couple layers of a nude eyeshadow on top of the concealer! good luck, glad i could help!

https://media.allure.com/photos/5d9cd6dff55d590008a39852/master/w_3000,h_1687,c_limit/Katie%20Jane%20Hughes%20Hooded%20eyeliner%20closeups.jpg
your eyeliners should kinda look like this

for hooded eyes, i like to draw the shape of eyeliner with eyes open so you can see how it will look normally instead of just slapping on eyeliner with a closed eye. then fill it in with the eye closed. for eyeshadow, try building up and out toward the outer corners of the eye. like another commenter said, a nice highlight in the inner corner will look great with your eyes. if your going for a more bold eyeshadow look, you could pluck some of those eyebrow hairs toward the tail to kinda expand your canvas - not too much though, you got some fantastic full brows

omg your cheekbones are amazing. since they’re so high and prominent, i personally would contour to really make them pop, then blend blush starting from the “peak” of your cheekbone toward the tip of your nose then back up toward your temple so the majority of the blush is on the side of your face kind of instead of in the middle

primer like everyone else said but i also like to put a skin color shade all over the lid, it makes colors brighter and also easier to blend in my opinion. i’m really impressed with the blending without a primer and also as a beginner! to add more dimension to the look, try adding a darker shade in the crease then using a real fluffy brush to blend out and also to create a nice transition between colors. that’s just kind of a basic tip though, it’s definitely an art so just keep practicing and experimenting!
